stories.body: Flights to and from Riyadh have been suspended after repeated Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport, with several international carriers extending cancellations through October 19. Saudi authorities said a projectile struck Terminal 4 on Sunday, killing one person and injuring 11, a day after a missile attack reportedly killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. The Saudi-led coalition has promised a firm response, while the Houthis said Saudi strikes hit Sana'a and warned airlines and passengers to avoid Saudi airports. The escalating attacks risk widening the regional consequences of the US-Iran war and threaten Saudi Arabia's ambitions to become a global aviation hub.
stories.headline: Houthi attacks disrupt Riyadh flights as Saudi-led coalition weighs a new Yemen operation

stories.body: A merchant ship sank after drone attacks just outside Bulgarian territorial waters, leaving 11 crew members missing and one sailor rescued, Bulgarian officials said. A second vessel, the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, was struck by three drones about 18 nautical miles offshore; all 15 crew members were rescued and five received medical care. Prime Minister Rumen Radev summoned Russia's ambassador, saying there was no conclusive evidence of responsibility but that the outcome benefited Russia. NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance would continue monitoring the Black Sea security situation and adjust its deterrence posture as needed.
stories.headline: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, prompting diplomatic fallout with Russia

stories.body: The International Monetary Fund raised its 2026 global growth forecast slightly to 3.1%, saying the economy had proved more resilient than expected amid the Middle East conflict. But the IMF warned that emergency oil inventories are dwindling, public debt and budget deficits limit governments' ability to cushion consumers from future price shocks, and new geopolitical disruptions could quickly affect supply and prices. It said countries not benefiting from the AI boom are especially exposed to energy shocks, uncertainty and mounting debt, and urged policymakers to rebuild supply capacity and fiscal buffers rather than merely cope with current pressures.
stories.headline: IMF upgrades global growth outlook but warns war, debt and energy risks threaten resilience

stories.body: Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital for surgery to remove a small lung nodule found during a recent check-up. The 71-year-old pope said the growth was well-contained and detected early, and Vatican officials described the procedure as low risk, though it will determine whether the nodule is malignant. His appointments have been cancelled through October 20. It is his first hospitalization since becoming pope in May 2025, and he is expected to remain at Gemelli's private-patient wing rather than its papal suite, which is under renovation.
stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV is hospitalized for surgery to remove an early-stage lung nodule

stories.body: A large-scale cyberattack disrupted refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, raising some fridge and freezer temperatures as high as 50C and spoiling fresh and frozen food. Intermarché and Netto reported at least 300 affected shops, Cooperative U more than 100, and Carrefour, Monoprix and E. Leclerc also reported incidents; some stores experienced fires. Authorities said attackers remotely triggered forced defrosting in systems using outdated software, and France's cybersecurity agency is investigating a possible vulnerability in software supplied by Denmark's Danfoss. Retailers said losses could run to tens of millions of euros in a single day.
stories.headline: Cyberattack on French supermarkets spoils food in hundreds of stores

stories.body: Federal agents searched Democratic Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington home as part of an ongoing investigation into alleged immigration fraud, according to reports. Homeland Security Investigations, the investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security, carried out the search. The inquiry reportedly includes immigration paperwork completed by Omar's late father when she was a child. Omar accused the Trump administration of using government institutions to intimidate and target political opponents.
stories.headline: Federal agents search Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington home in immigration-fraud investigation

stories.body: Voters in 10 states will consider ballot measures involving school prayer, transgender athletes and other education disputes. Some of the initiatives seek constitutional amendments, which could make their effects more durable than ordinary legislation. The votes will test how far education culture-war issues can be settled directly at the ballot box during the midterm cycle.
stories.headline: Education culture-war measures, including school prayer and transgender-athlete rules, head to state ballots

stories.body: A sixth person who had measles has died in Pennsylvania, according to a local coroner, as the state endures the country's worst ongoing outbreak. The outbreak has surpassed 1,000 reported cases, making it the first in the United States to exceed that threshold since 1991.
stories.headline: Pennsylvania measles outbreak reaches a sixth reported death and more than 1,000 cases

stories.body: Democrats are increasingly framing corruption as an explanation for high housing, health-care and everyday costs as they campaign for the midterms. A national survey commissioned by Democratic-aligned groups found that linking corruption to economic struggles increased support for Democratic congressional candidates by about three percentage points, while Democrats and allied groups have spent roughly $104 million on ads mentioning corruption since April. Strategists say the message works best when it connects a rigged political system to a rigged economy rather than focusing solely on President Donald Trump, though Republicans argue Democrats lack credibility on the issue.
stories.headline: Democrats make corruption and cost of living a central midterm message

stories.body: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited Ceuta in the first trip there by a Spanish head of state since 2007 and Felipe's first since taking the throne. The visit came two and a half months after a large influx of migrants from Morocco, and the monarchs were greeted by hundreds of residents before meeting local authorities, visiting a school and attending an event for civil society. They were also due to pay tribute at the Sidi Embarek cemetery to around 140 people who died while trying to swim from Morocco to Ceuta. Morocco responded with official silence rather than the public condemnation it voiced during the 2007 royal visit.
stories.headline: Spain's king and queen visit Ceuta amid migration pressures and renewed tensions with Morocco

stories.body: Spain's Supreme Court upheld the temporary suspension of voting rights for 163,020 people granted Spanish nationality as descendants of Civil War exiles under the Democratic Memory Law, leaving them unable to vote in the November 29 general election. The court rejected requests from the state legal service and prosecutors to lift the measure, saying the interest in preserving the integrity of the electoral roll outweighed the affected citizens' voting rights. The ruling creates major logistical problems for electoral authorities and consulates, which had said it was materially impossible to review the affected registrations in time, and the government is considering an appeal to the Constitutional Court.
stories.headline: Spain's Supreme Court maintains suspension of voting rights for thousands naturalized under the Democratic Memory Law

stories.body: The Broad Front, formed by Movimiento Sumar, United Left, Más Madrid and Comuns, has selected former Barcelona mayor Ada Colau as its candidate for prime minister ahead of Spain's November 29 election. The coalition has kept the door open to Podemos, but the left remains divided after Podemos reached a separate collaboration agreement with ERC. Under that deal, Podemos will not run in Catalonia while ERC will include figures close to Podemos on its lists and campaign alongside Irene Montero. Parties have until October 16 to register electoral coalitions.
stories.headline: Ada Colau is named the Broad Front's candidate as Spain's left remains divided before the November election

stories.body: Spain's government is set to approve the creation of 500 new judicial posts and 200 prosecutor posts through two royal decrees. The expansion would increase the judicial workforce by 7.8% and the public prosecution service by 6.6%, according to Justice Ministry sources. It is the government's second major planned increase in these legal workforces.
stories.headline: Spain approves a second major expansion of its judicial and prosecutorial workforce

stories.body: High-speed trains between Barcelona and Madrid will continue using a single track over a stretch of more than 20 kilometres for the next several days after a train caught fire between Ricla and Plasencia de Jalón in Zaragoza. Renfe said the burned train cannot be removed until the coming days, after which infrastructure manager Adif must repair damaged overhead cables and certify the section as safe. The restriction is expected to keep causing delays across the high-speed corridor.
stories.headline: High-speed rail disruption between Barcelona and Madrid continues after a train fire affects thousands

stories.body: Barcelona Metro will add service on Lines 1 and 5 from October 15, aiming to reduce Saturday wait times to around five minutes. TMB will add two trains on Saturdays between 10 a.m. and 9 p.m., while Line 5 will also gain an extra train during weekday afternoon peak hours. The operator said the change responds to rising demand: Saturday validations in the affected periods have risen by nearly 10% on Line 1 since 2023 and almost 15% on Line 5.
stories.headline: Barcelona Metro will increase Saturday service on Lines 1 and 5 to five-minute intervals

stories.body: Barcelona's Vall d'Hebron Hospital has used a minimally invasive procedure to reopen blocked portal veins in 12 of 24 children treated since 2018, allowing many to avoid complex open surgery. The blockage can cause portal hypertension, enlarged spleens, low platelet counts and potentially life-threatening digestive bleeding. Doctors use two small punctures, through the spleen and liver, to guide catheters to the blocked vein, widen it with balloons and place a stent. Ten of the successfully treated children still have an open vein, and the hospital says success rates in more recent cases have approached 70%.
stories.headline: Vall d'Hebron pioneers a minimally invasive treatment for blocked portal veins in children
